correctness.rationale: Decomposing each selected set into edge-vertices C and original vertices T, total domination of original vertices forces C to be an edge cover. Other edge-vertices are dominated except isolated edges in (V,C); each isolated edge demands a T choice from its endpoints. For any non-perfect-matching cover, at least one unrestricted original vertex flips the signed sum to zero. For a matching each pair gives signed coefficient -1 which cancels edge-vertex sign. This proves the multivariate identity and ordinary enumerator for all finite simple graphs, including isolated vertices; independent exhaustive 760 signed edge selectors across all labelled graphs n<=4 corroborate. No efficient counting claim.

value.rationale: The multivariate identity exactly transforms a natural all-total-domination signed generating function into the well-studied perfect-matching polynomial, giving coefficientwise cancellation, an unexpected nonnegativity at z=-1, and a family of algebraic identities. It is mathematically useful beyond computing one graph.

final_claim: Every finite simple middle graph has a multivariate signed total-domination polynomial equal to the original graph’s perfect-matching polynomial, with full edge-cover ordinary enumeration.
limitations: A signed domination identity for middle graphs may appear in older combinatorial or neighborhood-hypergraph literature outside the inspected primary papers.
